title: Microbuffer price ↔ headcount coupling scratchbook
content:
Purpose:
Quick exploratory workbook / scratchpad to capture experiments coupling short-term price moves with headcount phasing and a small reserved capacity buffer ("microbuffer") for burst/latency-critical customers. Not a commitment doc — rough math and open questions.

Summary notes (TL;DR):
- We model a small microbuffer (2–6% of committed GPU capacity) that can be funded either by price tilt (temporary surcharge) or by accelerating hiring of on-call contractors.
- Primary trade: raise per-token price slightly (10% band) vs hire additional SRE/ops capacity (contractor FTE equivalents) to meet SLA without throttling during spikes.
- This doc contains baseline assumptions, 3 scenario runs, a headcount phasing sketch, quick unit-econ sensitivity, and immediate action items.

Key assumptions (baseline):
- Current monthly committed GPU cost (cash outflow to cloud/leases): $1,800,000 per month.
- Effective tokens served (hosted API + dedicated + private pockets): 12B tokens / month baseline (mix: 70% hosted, 20% dedicated, 10% private).
- Average revenue per 1k tokens today: $0.40 (weighted across customers).
- On-call contractor cost to add 1 FTE-equivalent (capacity ops, spot booking + monitoring): $32k / month loaded (includes contractors/agency premium).
- Microbuffer target capacity: absorb 15% token spike for 4 hours daily or 40% spike for 30 minutes. Equivalent monthly-capacity cost approximated as 3% of committed GPU cost when sized conservatively.

Quick unit-econ baseline math (rounded):
- Monthly revenue (baseline) = 12B tokens / 1000 * $0.40 = $4,800,000
- Gross margin before ops (naive) = revenue - GPU cost = $3,000,000
- Add ops/infra/salary bucket ~= $1,400,000 -> operating margin ~ $1,600,000

Scenarios (one-page sensitivity):
1) Price tilt + small microbuffer (Conservative)
   - Price increase: +10% across hosted API only (hosted is 70% of volume) -> blended price increase = 0.7 * 10% = +7% rev -> new rev ≈ $5.136M (+$336k)
   - Allocate 60% of incremental revenue to microbuffer reserve and ops (first 3 months) -> $201k / month for microbuffer/ops; remaining incremental revenue used to cushion margins.
   - No new headcount hires; rely on auto-scaling + buffer.
   - Expected result: runway extension ~ 6–8 weeks at current burn cadence vs baseline. Customer churn risk: low unless price-sensitive customers in hosted tier (investigate top-10).

2) Hiring-first (Ops expansion)
   - Hire 4 contractor FTE equivalents quickly to improve incident handling and shore up runbooks; cost ≈ $128k / month.
   - Fund microbuffer via capacity reallocation (burst credits) instead of price; rely on on-call ops to triage spikes.
   - Revenue unchanged; margins drop by $128k/month. Expected runway: slightly compressed; lower churn risk vs price tilt but higher cash burn.

3) Hybrid: modest price tilt + partial hiring + lean buffer
   - Price tilt +5% hosted (+3.5% blended) -> incremental rev ≈ $168k
   - Hire 2 contractors ($64k/m) and earmark $80k for microbuffer credits. Net improvement to gross margin small but provides both operational and price cushions.

Scenario table (compact):
- Baseline revenue: $4.8M | GPU cost: $1.8M | Ops inc: $1.4M | Net: $1.6M
- S1 (price10): rev:+$336k | ops inc:+$0 | microbuffer funded from rev:$201k | net change:+$135k
- S2 (hire4): rev:+$0 | ops inc:+$128k | microbuffer funded by reallocation: $0 | net change:-$128k
- S3 (hybrid): rev:+$168k | ops inc:+$64k | microbuffer:$80k | net change:+$24k

Headcount phasing sketch (12-week sprint view):
- Week 0: decision point. Mobilize hiring vendor if hire path chosen.
- Weeks 1–4: contractor onboarding and runbook sprint. Two-week SLO focus: prefix/KV cache improvements to reduce burst-cost.
- Weeks 5–8: stress-run simulation with traffic replay from last 90 days. Tune batching and cache sizing.
- Weeks 9–12: stability review + conversion playbook for contractors to perm if impact >= target. Metrics review: token latency P99, cost per 1k tokens, incident MTTR.

Microbuffer sizing quick calc (back-of-envelope):
- 3% of committed GPU cost = $54k / month. This funds short-duration bursts via spot/credits; if top-up needed during multi-day events, escalate to price tilt or draw from credit line.
- If microbuffer doubled -> 6% = $108k / month -> can absorb larger or longer spikes.

Customer sensitivity considerations (open list):
- Which hosted customers are price elastic? (Action: ask growth for hosted cohort price-sensitivity by top-50 by revenue; rough segmentation: internal hypothesis: 60% low-elasticity, 30% medium, 10% high).
- Contract clauses for Dedicated customers — can we temporarily throttle or move non-critical workloads during spikes? (Legal ops: flag).
- Private deployments SLA implications: customers with on-prem/private contracts might expect no price movement; risk of churn if we change public pricing tiers.

Open questions / TODOs: (short-term, owners)
- [ ] (Rajat) Pull top-20 hosted customers usage & price-sensitivity (due 2025-11-10).
- [ ] (Marisol) Legal check for variability clause for small temporary surcharge and whether we can apply to new sign-ups vs existing customers (due 2025-11-07).
- [ ] (Dmitri) Run replay for 2025-09 token spike and estimate microbuffer drawdown under baseline config (due 2025-11-12).
- [ ] (Finance) Build three-scenario P&L sheet with week-by-week cash flows for 12 weeks (owner: Avery) — include capex if any (due 2025-11-14).

Risks and mitigations: 
- Reputational risk from price changes -> mitigation: targeted, time-bound surcharge, clear communications, and trial on new customers only.
- Cash risk from hiring-first approach -> mitigation: prefer contractors with short notice terms; include conversion clause.
- Operational risk if microbuffer not sufficient -> mitigation: enable emergency fallback to heavier quantization profiles and narrower batching parameters, temporary degraded SLO for low-tier customers.

Quick comms drafts (skeleton):
- Internal note to Sales/CS: "We are testing a short-term microbuffer strategy to stabilize latency during demand spikes. No changes to existing enterprise contracts without Sales + Legal signoff. We'll pilot a modest 10% hosted surcharge on new signups or opt-in customers for 8 weeks."
- External (if enacted): short email and Dashboard banner for impacted hosted customers with clear expiration date and credits toward future invoices.

Appendix: mini-sensitivity table (impact on margin by % price shift on hosted tier)
- hosted-price +5% -> blended rev +3.5% -> rev +$168k -> net margin +$84k (after 50% earmark)
- hosted-price +10% -> blended rev +7% -> rev +$336k -> net margin +$168k (after 40% earmark)
- hosted-price -5% -> blended rev -3.5% -> rev -$168k -> net margin -$168k (worse)

Notes to self: keep this lightweight. The point is to make a crisp decision by Week 0 (decision point). Prefer Hybrid unless top-20 hosted customers show high elasticity.

Choppy brainstorm fragments (scratchpad):
- Could we do a token-based surcharge only above baseline 95th percentile daily usage? (metered surcharge instead of blanket).
- Use opt-in premium for guaranteed low-latency with explicit extra fee -> upsell to high-SLA customers.
- Quantization push on non-critical model variants for burst windows to reduce GPU wall-clock cost.
- Consider temporary traffic-shaping rules: non-critical requests can be queued with small delay for 2–10% of requests during spikes.

End of scratchbook. Keep in drive; convert to formal proposal if S1/S3 favored.
